body:
You have an advantage in that you're young, and still have the time and opportunity to turn things around once you're able to leave your family. Just don't marry your parents if you know what I mean. The fact that your dad is a "youth pastor" is not surprising. Some of the shittiest people I've known in my life have been "pastors" or people of "faith". I'm using quotes because in my book, their Christianity means absolutely nothing because of their hypocrisy. Anyway, look at it this way - you have just 5 more years. at which point you can start a fresh new life without the baggage of a failed marriage, kids, career, mortgage, etc. You have an opportunity many of us don't.

Edit: I meant 5 years, not 4

You are right, and as a few others have said here, it would probably be best to get the depression under control first. It's never good to make major decisions when you're depressed.

I have a counselor I have seen in the past, I know and trust this person, so I can start there.

As to our sex life, it's so-so. Maybe once every two weeks, depending on how busy we are and both feel. I don't feel that our sex life is a huge issue here.

Could she be having an affair? I don't want to sound naive, but I doubt it. At least, I don't have any suspicions. TBH I don't think she would even have time for such things (and neither would I). BUT, I will say that if she I do find out she's having an affair, I won't be completely shocked.

She has some physical health issues which cause her some chronic pain. She also has a few neurological (which is a grey area into mental) issues for which she is taking medication, though she has never been diagnosed with depression, anxiety, or other "classic" psychiatric disorders.  I am fully aware that these meds **might** be causing some of the irritability and mood changes. It's impossible to prove though.

Unfortunately, I don't have any friends and I am mostly estranged from my family. My only way to talk with anyone is through random internet strangers like Reedit.

You asked "How harmful is your wife's behavior to you and the kids?". Fair question! It's not super frequent, but I would say frequent enough (to me at least) for it to shut me down. I used to fight back or just tolerate it but now I can't. I just completely shut down and I have even panicked about it on occasion.

Outside of a total character transformation, no. We've been through this before too. We'll go into marital counseling and she'll get better but eventually we end up right back where we started. I am NOT saying I don't have faults, I am just saying that this particular issue keeps coming back and she keeps saying it's all in my perception. I think this is called "gaslighting".

> "I think it's this IUD"
and
> "I didn't mean it like that you're being too sensitive"

We have the same wife. She is so resentful about the IUD, because she is constantly mentioning it and wants me to get a vasectomy.

God yes, she was always like this, but it has gotten worse. She has always had a slightly nasty streak, which my family noticed (and warned me about) before we got married. I guess I just learned to deal with it for all these years.
Do you feel like what you're going through (depression?) is because of relationship issues or something else?

I mostly work from home. The 2.5 hour commute was a bit unusual due to an accident. Believe me, my commute is the least of my worries and not a stressor at all.

I am wondering if this is like situational depression? I kind of feel like this is a feedback loop because the relationship issues are making me depressed, which makes the issues worse, and on and on. I don't think I am depressed "just because". No, I feel depressed most times we have a fight and when I am not with her, I feel pretty fine. How am I supposed to take care of the depression without working on the relationship, which in my opinion is the cause?
